title: Initial investigation & USG approach
guide: The initial triad (USG abdomen, RFT with urea/creatinine/Na+/K+, urine analysis with preferred 24hr protein), the size/CMD algorithm (<8 cm, 8-10 cm loss of CMD, >10 cm loss of CMD in DM/HIV/amyloidosis), normal-kidney echogenicity and the CKD end-points.

title: CKD mimics & the AKI arm
guide: Rule out hydronephroureteronephrosis before labelling CKD, then the tempo-based non-CKD split: hours-days AKI (postrenal/pre-renal/ATN/AIN) with the prerenal normal-urine clue.

title: RPRF, vascular causes & RAS introduction
guide: Days-weeks RPRF (RPGN m/c by biopsy; severe ATN/TMA rare), the hypertensive-crisis vascular branch (RAS large-vessel vs TMA small-vessel), the normal-RFT trio, and RAS aliases and its progression to CKD/ischemic nephropathy.

title: RAS: most common causes & Goldblatt model
guide: Cause-by-population table (atherosclerosis proximal 1-2 cm >80% occlusion; FMD mid-distal; Takayasu F:M 9:1 proximal; PAN young males entire length with microaneurysm), the two-kidney-one-clip model and the asymmetric-kidney entry point.

title: Unilateral RAS pathogenesis
guide: Both limbs of the unilateral diagram: affected kidney (↓RBF → renin → aldosterone → AT-II ↑↑ → vasoconstriction → HTN) vs normal kidney (↑RBF/↑RIHP → ↓PCT reabsorption → pressure natriuresis), plus vasoconstrictor potency and the persistent-HTN/normal-basic-Ix picture.

title: RAS investigations & unilateral treatment
guide: USG asymmetric kidney → renal doppler screen → CT/MR angiography IOC; ACEi/ARBs as DOC and PTRA only when the kidney is >8 cm.

title: Bilateral RAS: pathogenesis & treatment
guide: Poor prognosis; loss of pressure natriuresis/↓RIHP → Na+/H2O retention → volume overload → flash pulmonary edema with (−) renin feedback; B/L PTRA with stenting; diuretics DOC with ACEi/ARBs C/I; stop smoking and statins.

title: CDU screening values & fibromuscular dysplasia
guide: CDU with parvus tardus, RI ≥ 0.8 → CKD vs RI < 0.8 with PSV >180 cm/s / RAR >3.5 / ΔRI >0.05 → CT/MR IOC and conventional angiography gold standard; FMD's young-girl epidemiology, medial fibroplasia, 25% bilateral/25% cerebral, string-of-beads and PTRA.
